method_as_stated: THEORY: a tangential contact force along the relative tangential surface velocity, of general amplitude f(u, r), with the multiplicative noise that restores the Boltzmann distribution derived for the Ito, Stratonovich and Hanggi-Klimontovich conventions. Three friction laws: linear (w(r) gamma_f u; the noise is then additive and the pair acts as a DPD-like thermostat that couples rotation and translation), Coulomb (w(r) kappa_f) and Coulomb-Newton (the smaller of the two), with w(r) = -dU_WCA/dr. Spinning friction and static (memory) friction are left out. SIMULATION ENGINES: HOOMD-blue for the equilibrium-consistency tests and the pressure-driven flows; LAMMPS for the motility-induced phase separation study. The HOOMD code was merged into HOOMD-blue and is documented in version 6.1.0 as hoomd.md.pair.friction (https://hoomd-blue.readthedocs.io/en/v6.1.0/hoomd/md/pair/module-friction.html); data and LAMMPS/HOOMD scripts at doi 10.48328/tudatalib-1838 (version 3). Integration is Euler-forward on the stochastic forces (the Ito convention). PARTICLES: identical masses m, radii sigma/2, moment of inertia (2/5) m R^2, WCA repulsion. CONSISTENCY TESTS: 2D at area fraction 0.6 and 3D at volume fraction 0.3, 10,000 particles, periodic, units t0 = sqrt(m sigma^2/kT), gamma_R = pi kT t0 and gamma = 3 pi kT t0/sigma^2 (a sphere in a unit-viscosity fluid), WCA epsilon = kT; equilibrated 20 t0 and sampled 200 t0 at time step 0.001 t0 (linear and Coulomb-Newton) or 0.0001 t0 (Coulomb); each friction law run with and without the frictional noise. FLOWS: no coupling to a background medium (gamma = gamma_R = 0) and no solvent hydrodynamics; walls of immobilised particles (mass 1e10 m) on a square lattice of spacing sigma at y = +/- 8.5847 sigma plus a Gaussian roughness delta_w; 10,000 particles at volume fraction 0.15 in an accessible volume 151.694 x 15.1694 x 15.1694 sigma^3, periodic in x and z; time step 0.001 t0, 500 t0 to steady state, 6,000 t0 sampled; bulk force 0.01 kT/sigma (0.02 checked for linearity); Coulomb-Newton with kappa_f = 5 and gamma_f from 0.2 to 6 kT t0/sigma^2; Couette runs with walls at +/- 1 sigma/t0 to separate slip length from the hydrodynamic boundary (Allen's procedure). MIPS (LAMMPS): 20,000 two-dimensional active Langevin particles, time unit t_R = gamma_R/kT, gamma = t_R kT/sigma^2, mass 0.05 kT (t_R/sigma)^2, WCA epsilon = 10 kT, Coulomb-Newton gamma_f = 1 kT t_R/sigma^2 and kappa_f = 1, time step 1e-5 t_R, periodic; MIPS identified by a bimodal local-density histogram (AMEP).
